4. FETAL MONITORING DURING LABOUR

128.FHR monitoring is a guidance tool on fetal condition and not a diagnostic test.
129.Findings of FHR monitoring should be assessed along with clinical picture
130.Decisions are based on clinical picture along with FHR monitoring but never alone on FHR findings.
131.Women’s decision should be respected
132.Maintain one to one support
133.Increased intervention with continuous CTG as compared to intermittent auscultation.

Initial assessment during labour:

134.Assessment of risks
135.Review ANC record
136.Women’s preferences and method of fetal assessment discussed with her during antenatal period.
137.Discuss with women that risk assessment is a continuous process so, FHR monitoring tool may change during the course of labour.

Intermittent Auscultation – IA:

138.Offer to low risk women
139.Use either pinard stethoscope or Doppler USG
140.Carry out Intermittent Auscultation after a palpated contraction
141.For 1 min
142.Every 15 min in 1st stage and every 5 min in 2nd stage
143.Record o Partogram as single rate
144.Record accelerations and decelerations if heard.
145.Palpate maternal pulse and record 1 hourly and more oftenly if there are any concerns.
146.Ensure differentiation between the maternal and fetal heartbeat.
147.No fetal heart beat => urgent real time USG assessment.

Concerns about differentiating between fetal and maternal heart rates => seek help and consider changing the method of FHR monitoring.

148.In 2nd stage it is easier to mistakenly auscultate maternal rather than FHR

Important Consideration while Reviewing CTG:

149.Evaluate changes on trace over time
150.Document any change from previous review
151.Review changes alongside existing or new intrapartum risk factors
152.Think about possible reason for any change and take into account whole clinical picture in formulating ongoing care.
153.Normal CTG trace indicate that baby is coping well with labour
154.Changes to FHR during labour are common and don’t necessarily cause concern, however they may represent fetal compromise.
155.If CTG trace changes or is not normal there will be less certainly about the condition of the baby

Accelerations:

156.Transient in FHR of 15bpm or more lasting 15 sec or more
157.Presence of accelerations even with reduced variability is reassuring.
158.Absence of accelerations on an otherwise normal CTG trace does not indicate fetal acidosis.

Categorization of CTG traces:

159.Normal
-No amber or no red feature
-All 4 features are white.
160.Suspicious:
-Any 1 feature amber
161.Pathological
-Any feature red or
-2 or more features are amber.

Special consideration for CTG traces in 2nd stage of labour:

162.Interpretation more challenging in 2nd stage
163.Keep low threshold for seeking 2nd opinion
164.Differentiate FHR from MHR every 5 min
165.Consider scalp electrode if there is concern

about confusing FHR and MHR.

166.Accelerations are most likely to be maternal pulse
167.If there are deceleration, look for other signs of hypoxia like in baseline FHR or reduction in variability.
168.Hypoxia is more common and more rapid in active 2nd stage
⇨FHR > 20bPm from baseline or more from start of labour is labelled as red feature in active.
169.CTG concern in 2nd stage.

 

 

170.Obtain obstetric review

171.Discourage Pushing
172.Discontinue oxytocin infusion unless birth is imminent
173.Agree and document CTG trace.

181.Exclude acute events
-Cord prolapses

Record keeping for CTG:

198.Set date and time clock correctly on machine
199.Set paper speed at 1cm/ min
200.Correct labelling with women’s name, DOB, NHS Number, Pulse rate @ start of monitoring and date of CTG
201.Save record Electronically or photocopy of CTG trace
202.Keep record for 25 years
203.Sustained possible brain injury to baby => store CTG indefinitely.
